policies.title: Password Reset
policies.summary: Employees can reset password via self-service portal; manual unlock by IT required if locked after 5 failed attempts.
policies.source_text: Employees can reset their own password via the self-service portal at any time. If locked out after 5 failed attempts, contact IT to unlock the account manually. No approval required.
conditions: Self-service password reset is permitted at any time
Account lockout is automatically triggered after 5 failed login attempts
Locked accounts require manual intervention by IT Helpdesk
allowed_actions: Self-service password reset via portal
Manual account unlock by IT Helpdesk
prohibited_actions: Resetting locked account (>5 failed attempts) via self-service portal
resolution_steps: Direct user to self-service portal at https://identity.veridian-corp.example/self-service/reset
If locked out due to >5 failed attempts, dispatch manual unlock request to IT Helpdesk
Verify identity and confirm account unlock; no managerial approval required
policies.time_constraints: Immediate self-service; manual IT unlock SLA: 15 minutes

policies.title: VPN Access
policies.summary: Automatic VPN for full-time employees; manager approval via form for contractors; 90-day credential renewal.
policies.source_text: VPN access is granted automatically to all full-time employees. Contractors require manager approval submitted via the access request form. VPN credentials expire every 90 days and must be renewed by the employee.
conditions: Full-time employees receive automatic VPN access
Contractors require manager approval submitted via access request form
VPN credentials expire every 90 days and must be renewed by the employee
allowed_actions: Automatic VPN provisioning for full-time employees
Employee self-service 90-day credential renewal
Submission of contractor access request form by manager
prohibited_actions: Granting VPN access to contractors without verified manager approval
Bypassing the 90-day credential expiration requirement
resolution_steps: Verify requester employment type (full-time employee vs contractor)
For full-time employees: confirm identity and guide employee through 90-day credential renewal portal
For contractors: verify submission of official access request form and confirmation of manager sign-off
Provision or extend VPN credentials upon verified authorization
policies.time_constraints: Credentials valid for 90 days; contractor approval turnaround 1-2 business days

policies.title: Laptop Replacement
policies.summary: Eligible for replacement after 3 years or earlier for verified hardware failure; requires 2 weeks advance notice.
policies.source_text: Laptops are eligible for replacement after 3 years of service, or earlier in case of verified hardware failure. Requests must be raised at least 2 weeks in advance of intended replacement.
conditions: Laptop must have reached at least 3 years of service from date of issue
Early replacement before 3 years requires verified hardware failure confirmed by diagnostic review
Requests must be submitted at least 2 weeks in advance of intended replacement date
Interacts with Asset Management Policy (4-year refresh cycle requiring Finance sign-off if < 4 years)
required_approvals: Finance Sign-off (mandatory if < 4 years old per Asset Management Policy)
allowed_actions: Hardware replacement request with minimum 2 weeks advance notice
Hardware diagnostic evaluation for early failure claims
Hardware repair (without replacement) for devices < 3 years old without fatal hardware failure
prohibited_actions: Replacing laptops under 3 years old without verified hardware failure
Fulfilling laptop replacement with less than 2 weeks advance notice
Replacing laptops under 4 years old without Finance sign-off in addition to IT approval
resolution_steps: Verify laptop issue date and calculate current service age
If device is under 3 years: dispatch hardware diagnostic to check if repair is possible rather than replacement
If device is completely inoperable or >= 3 years: confirm 2-week notice window
If device is between 3 and 4 years: flag for dual IT approval and Finance sign-off per Asset Management Policy
Queue approved ticket to Hardware Depot for fulfillment
policies.time_constraints: Requests must be raised at least 2 weeks in advance; 3-year service eligibility

policies.title: Software Installation Requests
policies.summary: Approved catalog software can be self-installed; non-catalog software requires 3–5 business days IT Security review.
policies.source_text: Standard software (listed in the approved catalog) can be self-installed. Non-catalog software requires IT Security review, which takes 3–5 business days.
conditions: Standard software listed in approved company catalog can be self-installed without approval
Non-catalog software (including third-party tools and browser extensions) requires mandatory IT Security review
IT Security review takes 3–5 business days
allowed_actions: Self-installation of approved catalog software via corporate software center
Submission of non-catalog software review request to IT Security
prohibited_actions: Self-installation or unauthorized execution of non-catalog software
Bypassing the 3–5 business day IT Security review process
resolution_steps: Cross-reference requested software or extension against approved catalog
If in catalog: provide direct self-service download and installation instructions
If not in catalog: create non-catalog software review ticket, collect vendor details and business justification
Route ticket to IT Security Review queue with 3–5 business days SLA notice
policies.time_constraints: IT Security review requires 3–5 business days

policies.title: Printer Troubleshooting
policies.summary: Check queue and restart print spooler first; if issue persists, log ticket with printer asset tag.
policies.source_text: For printer issues, first check the printer queue and restart the print spooler. If the issue persists after restart, log a ticket with the printer’s asset tag.
conditions: User must first inspect printer queue and restart print spooler service
A ticket can only be logged if issue persists after queue check and spooler restart
Printer asset tag is a mandatory required field for logging a dispatch ticket
allowed_actions: Checking and clearing stuck print queue jobs
Restarting local Windows print spooler service
Logging dispatch ticket with validated printer asset tag
prohibited_actions: Dispatching floor technician without first attempting print spooler restart
Logging a printer ticket without an asset tag
resolution_steps: Instruct user to verify printer queue and clear any hung or stuck print jobs
Provide step-by-step guidance to restart the print spooler service
Ask user to test print after spooler restart
If problem persists, prompt user for printer asset tag (e.g. VER-PRN-XX-XX)
Log technician dispatch ticket once asset tag is provided
policies.time_constraints: Same-day technician triage upon ticket logging with asset tag

policies.title: Email Mailbox Quota
policies.summary: Default mailbox quota is 25GB; archive old mail; increases > 25GB require manager approval and are capped at 50GB.
policies.source_text: Default mailbox quota is 25GB. Employees nearing quota should archive old mail. Quota increases beyond 25GB require manager approval and are capped at 50GB.
conditions: Default mailbox quota is 25GB for all employees
Employees reaching quota must archive old emails and empty Deleted Items
Quota increases beyond 25GB require formal manager approval
Mailbox quota is strictly capped at 50GB maximum
allowed_actions: Archiving old mail to local or cloud archive store
Requesting quota increase up to 50GB with manager sign-off
prohibited_actions: Increasing mailbox quota beyond 50GB hard cap under any circumstances
Increasing mailbox quota beyond 25GB without written manager approval
resolution_steps: Verify current mailbox storage utilization against 25GB threshold
Provide mail archiving guidelines to free up primary storage
If storage expansion is necessary, verify requested quota does not exceed 50GB cap
Obtain manager sign-off before applying quota expansion
IT Exchange administrator applies quota increase upon manager approval
policies.time_constraints: Next business day provisioning upon manager sign-off; 50GB hard ceiling

policies.title: Guest Wi-Fi Access
policies.summary: Guest Wi-Fi credentials are valid for 24 hours and generated by any employee at the front-desk kiosk; no ticket required.
policies.source_text: Guest Wi-Fi credentials are valid for 24 hours and can be generated by any employee from the front-desk kiosk. No IT ticket required.
conditions: Guest Wi-Fi credentials are valid for exactly 24 hours
Any Veridian employee can generate guest credentials at front-desk kiosk
No IT support ticket is required
allowed_actions: Self-generation of guest Wi-Fi passes by employees at reception/front-desk kiosk
Temporary guest access for up to 24 hours
prohibited_actions: Creating IT support tickets for guest Wi-Fi passes
Sharing internal employee Wi-Fi credentials with external visitors
resolution_steps: Inform employee that guest Wi-Fi credentials do not require an IT ticket
Direct employee to front-desk kiosk located in office reception
Employee enters guest details at kiosk to generate 24-hour access pass
Mark issue as resolved via self-service guidance
policies.time_constraints: Credentials valid for 24 hours; instantaneous at kiosk

policies.title: Expense Software Access
policies.summary: Access to expense management tool is granted by Finance, not IT; IT only assists with technical/login issues once account exists.
policies.source_text: Access to the expense management tool is granted by Finance, not IT. IT can only assist with login/technical issues once an account already exists.
conditions: Account creation and access entitlement are owned and granted by Finance
IT cannot create, provision, or approve expense tool accounts
IT can only assist with login, credential, or browser technical issues once an account already exists
allowed_actions: Routing new expense tool account requests to Finance team
Troubleshooting authentication, session, or browser errors for existing verified accounts
prohibited_actions: IT provisioning or approving initial expense tool accounts
Granting privileged administrative access without business justification (see precedent TK-1050)
resolution_steps: Clarify whether employee has an existing provisioned account or requires new access
If new account required: redirect employee to Finance Department authorization portal
If account already exists: troubleshoot invalid credentials, browser cookies, or password reset
If admin access requested: require written business justification and formal approval per precedent TK-1050
policies.time_constraints: Finance provisioning SLA applies; IT login troubleshooting SLA 4 hours

policies.title: Security Incident Reporting
policies.summary: Report suspected phishing, malware, unauthorized access to security@veridian-corp.example immediately; NEVER forward to other employees.
policies.source_text: Any suspected phishing email, malware, or unauthorized access attempt must be reported to security@veridian-corp.example immediately and should not be forwarded to other employees.
conditions: Applies to suspected phishing, malware, ransomware, or unauthorized access attempts
Must be reported immediately to security@veridian-corp.example
CRITICAL PROHIBITION: Must NOT be forwarded to other employees under any circumstances
allowed_actions: Immediate reporting to security@veridian-corp.example with headers
Isolating suspected host or quarantining malicious message
Alerting teammates NOT to click or interact if email was previously forwarded
prohibited_actions: Forwarding suspected phishing emails or malware to other employees or distribution lists
Clicking links or opening attachments in suspicious emails
Entering corporate credentials on unverified external sites
resolution_steps: EMERGENCY CONTAINMENT: Instruct employee immediately to stop forwarding the email
If already forwarded to colleagues: advise urgent warning to recipients NOT to click or open attachments
Instruct employee to forward original email as an attachment ONLY to security@veridian-corp.example
Create Priority 1 (P1) Security Incident Ticket in Infosec queue
Notify SOC team for immediate domain blocking and email quarantine

policies.title: Work-From-Home Equipment
policies.summary: Employees working remotely > 3 days/wk eligible for one-time allowance (chair, monitor); requires manager sign-off and Finance processing; IT only ships post-approval.
policies.source_text: Employees working remotely more than 3 days/week are eligible for a one-time home office equipment allowance (chair, monitor). Requires manager sign-off and Finance processing — IT only handles the equipment shipping request once approved.
conditions: Employee must work remotely more than 3 days per week (minimum 4 days remote)
Benefit is a one-time home office equipment allowance
Eligible items are chair and monitor
Requires manager sign-off AND Finance budget processing
IT role is strictly limited to handling equipment shipping once approvals are completed
allowed_actions: Submitting home office equipment allowance application for eligible remote employees
IT dispatching equipment shipping order upon receipt of confirmed Finance processing
prohibited_actions: IT shipping home office equipment prior to Manager and Finance approval
Granting allowance to employees working remote <= 3 days per week
Claiming allowance multiple times (restricted to one-time benefit)
resolution_steps: Verify employee remote work schedule (> 3 days remote per week)
Confirm employee has not previously utilized one-time home office allowance
Direct employee to submit request for Manager sign-off
Route manager-approved request to Finance for accounting and budget processing
Upon Finance sign-off, create IT Logistics ticket to ship monitor/chair to home address
policies.time_constraints: Shipping fulfilled within 2 business days after Finance processing sign-off

policies.title: Asset Management Policy (Extract)
policies.summary: All company-issued hardware follows standard 4-year refresh cycle; early replacement requires Finance sign-off in addition to IT approval.
policies.source_text: All company-issued hardware, including laptops and monitors, follows a standard 4-year refresh cycle from date of issue. Early replacement outside this cycle requires Finance sign-off in addition to IT approval.
conditions: Applies to all company-issued hardware including laptops and monitors
Standard refresh cycle is 4 years from date of issue
Early replacement outside 4-year cycle mandates dual sign-off: Finance sign-off AND IT approval
Interacts with KB-03: Laptops between 3 and 4 years old are eligible under KB-03 but require Finance sign-off under Asset Policy
required_approvals: Finance Sign-off (for all replacements outside 4-year refresh cycle)
allowed_actions: Standard lifecycle replacement at >= 4 years from date of issue
Early replacement with documented dual approval (IT + Finance)
prohibited_actions: Replacing company hardware < 4 years old without Finance sign-off
Bypassing IT asset audit before retirement of existing hardware
resolution_steps: Retrieve hardware serial number and original date of issue from asset registry
Calculate device age against the 4-year standard refresh threshold
If >= 4 years: schedule routine lifecycle hardware replacement
If < 4 years: create dual approval ticket requiring IT diagnostic justification and Finance budget sign-off
Dispatch hardware fulfillment only after dual authorization is recorded
policies.time_constraints: Standard 4-year refresh lifecycle from date of issue
